title: pr-retro-hard aggregation input
description: Input contract for aggregate_review.py. Every enumeration here is CLOSED and carries no catch-all member: an unknown value is a hard error, never a defaulted value. aggregate_review.py is the decision owner; this file is its data shape, and the two are asserted consistent by test_aggregate_review.py.

draft_digest.description: Digest of the semantic content of the draft under review. A finding whose recorded draft_digest differs from this value is stale and is not applied.

packet_digest.description: Digest of the review packet the voices were given. A finding whose recorded packet_digest differs from this value is stale and is not applied -- this catches the case where the packet's source material changed (e.g. a new PR commit landed) while the draft text itself did not.

original_confidence.description: This lesson's confidence before aggregation. Aggregation can only lower this, never raise it.

original_source.description: This lesson's source label before aggregation. Aggregation never rewrites this to cross-model: mob voices read one draft through one prompt and are correlated by construction, so their agreement is not independent cross-model evidence.

lessons.description: Keyed by lesson target (the same string used as a finding's `target`, e.g. `lesson-<key>`). Only targets with an entry here carry a confidence/source score; Q1-Q5 narrative targets and rule-draft-N targets are never scored -- dissent against them is still recorded (outcomes, consensus) but produces no confidence delta. Each target is scored independently: a dissent against one lesson never moves another lesson's confidence.

enable_demotion.description: Whether a demotion recommendation is acted on. Defaults to false: the recommendation is always computed and reported, but shipping in shadow mode means it changes no tier.

voice_kind.description: adversarial findings never count toward consensus and are reported separately.

round.description: Consensus is established only by an r1 finding on that exact (target, voice) pair. An r2 finding for a (target, voice) pair the same voice already spoke to in r1 supersedes it for scoring -- refuting, downgrading, or supplying a settling check the r1 finding lacked. An r2 finding for a NEW (target, voice) pair -- one that voice never spoke to in r1 -- never governs scoring; it is a new vote, which r2 cannot add.

target.description: What the finding is about, e.g. Q4 or lesson-<key> or rule-draft-2.

classification.description: Closed enumeration with no catch-all. UNSUPPORTED is the only classification that can produce a demotion recommendation, and only when its settling check is confirmed.

settling_check.description: A concrete check that would settle the finding: a command, a file:line reference, or a grep. The literal string (none) is a valid parsed value meaning no check was supplied.

draft_digest.description: The draft digest in force when this finding was produced. Compared against the top-level draft_digest to detect staleness.

packet_digest.description: The packet digest in force when this finding was produced. Compared against the top-level packet_digest to detect staleness, independent of draft_digest -- the packet's source material can change (a new PR commit lands) while the draft text stays fixed.

check_state.description: Five distinct states. unable_to_execute is NOT refuted: invalid evidence does not establish that the claim is false. refuted means the check was run and the claim did not hold -- it must not move confidence, count toward consensus, or recommend demotion, the same as if no check had been supplied.
